title: Queues
summary: First in, first out, and a deque when both ends move.

parts.rule: A queue is first-in, first-out. Enqueue at the back and dequeue at the front in O(1) with the right structure. A deque lets both ends push and pop. Breadth-first search and sliding windows that drop the oldest index are the classic consumers of this shape.

body:
Rule. A queue is first-in, first-out. Enqueue at the back and dequeue at the front in O(1) with the right structure. A deque lets both ends push and pop. Breadth-first search and sliding windows that drop the oldest index are the classic consumers of this shape.

Why it matters. Level-order tree walks and "process in arrival order" fail if you accidentally use a stack. Interview bugs include using a list pop from the front that is linear in some languages, or forgetting that BFS needs a queue so earlier nodes expand before later ones. Naming FIFO before coding is the tell that you picked the right structure.

Worked example. Breadth-first on a tiny graph: node 1 connects to 2 and 3; node 2 connects to 4. Start queue [1], seen {1}. Dequeue 1, enqueue 2 then 3 → queue [2, 3]. Dequeue 2, enqueue 4 → [3, 4]. Dequeue 3 (no new neighbors). Dequeue 4. Visit order is 1, 2, 3, 4 — grouped by distance from the start. If you had used a stack you would dive into 2 then 4 before ever seeing 3. For a sliding-window maximum of size 3 on values [1, 3, 2, 5], keep a deque of indices with decreasing values: after reading 5, stale indices leave the front and smaller candidates leave the back until the front holds the index of 5 as the window maximum.

[[diagram:fifo]]

When to use. Use a queue for BFS, task scheduling in arrival order, and producer-consumer buffers. Use a deque when the algorithm drops from the front and appends at the back, as in many sliding-window maximum templates. Use a bounded queue when backpressure is part of the design story.

When to refuse. Refuse a queue when the newest item must be handled first. Refuse implementing front removal as an O(n) shift when constant-time dequeue is required at scale. Refuse BFS with a stack "because both are sequences." Refuse a bounded queue without stating what happens on overflow or on a full buffer.
